topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, connects the material to preceding histology practicals, and outlines the lecture's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the history of tumor virology and explain how the study of transforming retroviruses revealed that oncogenes originate from altered host cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental assays for cell transformation and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the in vitro and in vivo assays used by cancer biologists to test whether specific genes or mutations can transform cells.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer genes and explain their genetic mechanisms of action and regulatory effects on the cell cycle.

topics.label: Types and mechanisms of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts, repair pathway defects, replication errors, and mitotic abnormalities that cause sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step genetic progression in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the Vogelstein model of stepwise mutation accumulation and chromosomal instability driving progression from benign lesions to metastatic cancer.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how inherited germline mutations accelerate tumorigenesis across various cancer syndromes and how selective pressure can drive secondary tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture, offers to take student questions, and suggests recommended reading.
